claim: The CA3 region of the hippocampus is the major site of sharp wave initiation.
source: The CA3 region of the hippocampus is the major site of sharp wave initiation, and a brain region crucially involved in learning and memory.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established fact about CA3.

claim: The CA3 region is crucially involved in learning and memory.
source: The CA3 region of the hippocampus is the major site of sharp wave initiation, and a brain region crucially involved in learning and memory.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established fact about CA3.

claim: Highly recurrent connectivity within the CA3 excitatory network is thought to underlie processes involved in memory formation.
source: Highly recurrent connectivity within its excitatory network is thought to underlie processes involved in memory formation.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical understanding in the field.

claim: Distinct subpopulations of pyramidal neurons within CA3 may contribute differently to network activity, including sharp waves.
source: Recent work has indicated that distinct subpopulations of pyramidal neurons within this region may contribute differently to network activity, including sharp waves, in CA3.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from recent work in the field.

claim: There is an asymmetry in the connectivity between thorny and athorny CA3 pyramidal cell populations.
source: Here, we disentangle the local connectivity between two distinct CA3 cell types in mice: thorny and athorny pyramidal cells. We find an asymmetry in the connectivity between these two populations, with athorny cells receiving strong input from both athorny and thorny cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract.

claim: Athorny cells receive strong input from both athorny and thorny cells.
source: We find an asymmetry in the connectivity between these two populations, with athorny cells receiving strong input from both athorny and thorny cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract.

claim: The thorny cell population receives very little input from the athorny population.
source: Conversely, the thorny cell population receives very little input from the athorny population.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract.

claim: The connectivity scheme between thorny and athorny cells may determine the sequential activation of these cell types during sharp waves.
source: Computational modeling suggests that this connectivity scheme may determine the sequential activation of these cell types during large network events such as sharp waves.
evidence: This is a conclusion from computational modeling presented in the study.

claim: The hippocampus has been established as an essential brain region for the formation of new memories since the study of patient H.M.
source: Since the study of patient H.M., the hippocampus has been established as an essential brain region for the formation of new memories (Scoville and Milner, 1957).
evidence: This is a well-established finding in neuroscience supported by a citation.

claim: Sharp wave-ripple complexes (SPW-Rs) are large network events characterised by the synchronous discharge of huge numbers of hippocampal CA3 pyramidal neurons.
source: SPW-Rs are large network events characterised by the synchronous discharge of huge numbers of hippocampal pyramidal (CA3) neurons (the sharp wave, SPW), followed by oscillatory activity downstream in the CA1 (ripple).
evidence: This is a description of SPW-Rs based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: During non-REM sleep, SPW-Rs essentially replay a compressed version of neural sequences that occurred during events preceding sleep.
source: During non-REM sleep, SPW-Rs essentially replay a compressed version of neural sequences that occurred during events preceding sleep (Wilson and McNaughton, 1994; Lee and Wilson, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: SPW-Rs play a key role in memory consolidation.
source: It is thought that these SPW-Rs play a key role in memory consolidation.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical understanding in the field.

claim: The CA3 region in the hippocampus is considered the main generator of SPWs.
source: The CA3 region in the hippocampus is considered the main generator of SPWs (Buzsáki, 1986).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Inhibition is proposed to be instrumental in SPW generation.
source: While inhibition is proposed to be instrumental in SPW generation, recent evidence has suggested that a subclass of pyramidal neurons may also play a pivotal role (Hunt et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a proposal in the field.

claim: A subclass of pyramidal neurons may play a pivotal role in SPW generation.
source: While inhibition is proposed to be instrumental in SPW generation, recent evidence has suggested that a subclass of pyramidal neurons may also play a pivotal role (Hunt et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to recent evidence.

claim: Diversity among pyramidal neuron populations is often overlooked when considering the role of these cells within neuronal circuits.
source: Diversity among pyramidal neuron populations is often overlooked when considering the role of these cells within neuronal circuits.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field.

claim: Several studies have reported functional and morphological heterogeneity within the pyramidal CA3 cell population.
source: However, several studies have reported functional and morphological heterogeneity within the pyramidal CA3 cell population (Bilkey and Schwartzkroin, 1990; Sun et al., 2017; Marissal et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Two distinct sub-types of CA3 pyramidal neurons are differentiated by the presence or absence of complex spine structures called thorny excrescences.
source: A recent study described two distinct sub-types of CA3 pyramidal neurons, differentiated by the presence or absence of complex spine structures called thorny excrescences (the post-synaptic site of input coming from mossy fibres of the dentate gyrus granule cells) (Hunt et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: Thorny excrescences are the post-synaptic site of input coming from mossy fibres of the dentate gyrus granule cells.
source: A recent study described two distinct sub-types of CA3 pyramidal neurons, differentiated by the presence or absence of complex spine structures called thorny excrescences (the post-synaptic site of input coming from mossy fibres of the dentate gyrus granule cells) (Hunt et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a definition of thorny excrescences.

claim: Cells lacking thorny excrescences, termed athorny pyramids, fire before thorny pyramids during SPWs.
source: The study showed that cells lacking these thorny excrescences, termed athorny pyramids, fire before thorny pyramids during SPWs (Hunt et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Athorny cells play an important role in SPW initiation and, in turn, in memory processing in CA3.
source: Therefore, it is proposed that athorny cells play an important role in SPW initiation and, in turn, in memory processing in CA3.
evidence: This is stated as a proposal based on previous findings.

claim: CA3 pyramidal cells connect to each other at a high rate (8.8%).
source: We have previously shown that CA3 pyramidal cells connect to each other at a high rate (8.8%) (Sammons et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Sub-type specific connectivity is crucial for the distinct firing times of athorny and thorny cells during SPWs.
source: When implementing this asymmetry into a computational model, we find that sub-type specific connectivity is crucial for the distinct firing times of athorny and thorny cells during SPWs.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the computational modeling in the study.

claim: 348 CA3 pyramids were recorded across the length of the CA3.
source: In total, we recorded from 348 CA3 pyramids across the length of the CA3 (CA3a: 20 cells, CA3b: 274 cells, CA3c: 54 cells).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental data collected.

claim: Of the 348 pyramids recorded, 229 were thorny and 119 were athorny.
source: Of these 348 pyramids, 229 were thorny and 119 were athorny (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental data and is shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Athorny cells tended to be located deeper in the pyramidal layer, towards the stratum oriens.
source: Furthermore, we found that athorny cells tended to be located deeper in the pyramidal layer, towards the stratum oriens.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: The findings on soma location and primary apical dendritic length resemble findings from Marissal et al., 2012 who observed similar differences between early and late born CA3 neurons.
source: These results resemble findings from Marissal et al., 2012 who observed similar differences in soma location and primary apical dendritic length between early and late born CA3 neurons, suggesting that thorny and athorny neurons may be developmentally distinct.
evidence: This is a comparison to previous research supported by a citation.

claim: Thorny and athorny neurons may be developmentally distinct.
source: These results resemble findings from Marissal et al., 2012 who observed similar differences in soma location and primary apical dendritic length between early and late born CA3 neurons, suggesting that thorny and athorny neurons may be developmentally distinct.
evidence: This is a suggestion based on comparison to previous research.

claim: There are differences in maximum firing rate, rheobase and input resistance between thorny and athorny cells.
source: We further found differences in maximum firing rate, rheobase and input resistance between thorny and athorny cells, but not in resting membrane potential (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is no difference in resting membrane potential between thorny and athorny cells.
source: We further found differences in maximum firing rate, rheobase and input resistance between thorny and athorny cells, but not in resting membrane potential (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is a high rate of connectivity (15%) between athorny cells.
source: We found a high rate of connectivity (15%) between athorny cells (Figure 2Ai), and from thorny onto athorny cells (11%; Figure 2Aii).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 2Ai.

claim: There is a connectivity rate of 11% from thorny onto athorny cells.
source: We found a high rate of connectivity (15%) between athorny cells (Figure 2Ai), and from thorny onto athorny cells (11%; Figure 2Aii).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 2Aii.

claim: Thorny cells connected to each other at a rate of 8%.
source: Thorny cells connected to each other at a rate of 8% (Figure 2Aiii).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 2Aiii.

claim: Connections from athorny onto thorny cells were the least common, occurring at a rate of 4%.
source: Meanwhile, connections from athorny onto thorny cells were the least common, occurring at a rate of 4% (Figure 2Aiv).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 2Aiv.

claim: The overall rate of connectivity (8.9%) corresponds well to the previously reported high level of connectivity within the general CA3 pyramidal population (8.8%).
source: The overall rate of connectivity (65/734 = 8.9%) corresponds well to our previously reported high level of connectivity within the general CA3 pyramidal population (8.8%) (Sammons et al., 2024).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous work by the authors supported by a citation.

claim: There were 2 reciprocally connected pairs of athorny-athorny neurons (4/92 connections = 4%).
source: We saw reciprocal connections between athorny-athorny pairs (2 reciprocally connected pairs; 4/92 connections = 4%) and thorny-thorny (2 reciprocally connected pairs; 4/362 connections = 1%) pairs of neurons.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: There were 2 reciprocally connected pairs of thorny-thorny neurons (4/362 connections = 1%).
source: We saw reciprocal connections between athorny-athorny pairs (2 reciprocally connected pairs; 4/92 connections = 4%) and thorny-thorny (2 reciprocally connected pairs; 4/362 connections = 1%) pairs of neurons.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: Synaptic connections were strongest amongst athorny-athorny cells, although no statistically significant differences were present across connection types.
source: Synaptic connections were strongest amongst athorny-athorny cells, although no statistically significant differences were present across connection types (Figure 2B, median [IQR] amplitudes for athorny-athorny: 1.08 [0.56] mV; ii, thorny-athorny: 0.88 [1.03] mV; iii, thorny-thorny: 0.57 [0.55] mV; iv, athorny-thorny: 0.66 [0.25] mV; p = 0.370, Kruskal-Wallis test).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: EPSPs across all connection types had latencies below 3 ms (with the exception of a single connection between two athorny cells which had a latency of 3.58 ms) indicating that identified connections were monosynaptic.
source: EPSPs across all connection types had latencies below 3 ms (with the exception of a single connection between two athorny cells which had a latency of 3.58 ms) indicating that identified connections were monosynaptic (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data with interpretation shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Athorny-athorny synapses had the lowest failure rate, although no statistical difference was observed between groups.
source: Athorny-athorny synapses had the lowest failure rate, although no statistical difference was observed between groups (Figure 2D, median [IQR] failure rate for athorny-athorny: 11.5 [20.5]%, thorny-athorny: 33.0 [36.2]%, thorny-thorny: 21.0 [36.3]%, athorny-thorny: 12.0 [47.5]%, p = 0.729, Kruskal-Wallis test).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Thorny-athorny connections show the highest synaptic product, followed by athorny-athorny connections.
source: Thorny-athorny connections show the highest synaptic product, followed by athorny-athorny connections (Figure 3Aiv).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 3Aiv.

claim: The results demonstrate a strong pattern of input onto athorny neurons and much weaker input onto thorny cells, particularly from the athorny sub-population.
source: Together, our results demonstrate a strong pattern of input onto athorny neurons and much weaker input onto thorny cells, particularly from the athorny sub-population (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings shown in Figure 3B.

claim: During SPW events, athorny (A) cells have been reported to fire before thorny (T) cells.
source: During SPW events, athorny (A) cells have been reported to fire before thorny (T) cells, suggesting that activity propagates in this direction (Hunt et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The model network includes two classes of interneurons: PV+ basket cells (B), which are active during SPWs, and a putative class of anti-SPW interneurons (C), which fire outside SPWs.
source: In addition to the two pyramidal cell populations, we included two classes of interneurons that have been suggested to play fundamental roles in SPW generation: PV+ basket cells (B), which are active during SPWs, and a putative class of anti-SPW interneurons (C), which fire outside SPWs, keeping the other populations inhibited (Evangelista et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a description of the computational model with a citation to previous work.

claim: Strong reciprocal coupling between the two inhibitory populations gives rise to a bistability between a SPW state and a non-SPW state.
source: Strong reciprocal coupling between the two inhibitory populations gives rise to a bistability between a SPW state and a non-SPW state, and the network alternates between these two states due to adaptation in pyramidal cells (Figure 4Bi), as proposed by Levenstein et al., 2019 as the driving mechanism of SPWs.
evidence: This is a description of the computational model with a citation to previous work and shown in Figure 4Bi.

claim: The network alternates between SPW and non-SPW states due to adaptation in pyramidal cells.
source: Strong reciprocal coupling between the two inhibitory populations gives rise to a bistability between a SPW state and a non-SPW state, and the network alternates between these two states due to adaptation in pyramidal cells (Figure 4Bi), as proposed by Levenstein et al., 2019 as the driving mechanism of SPWs.
evidence: This is a description of the computational model with a citation to previous work and shown in Figure 4Bi.

claim: Model parameters were tuned such that the SPW event incidence is ≈1/s and the average event duration is ≈80 ms.
source: We tuned model parameters (see Materials and methods) such that the SPW event incidence is ≈1/s (with stochastic onsets driven by finite-size fluctuations) and the average event duration is ≈80 ms (Figure 4Bi).
evidence: This is a description of the computational model parameters shown in Figure 4Bi.

claim: In the model simulations, A cells emit a larger number of early spikes due to a lower rheobase and a steeper f-I curve.
source: Among the two pyramidal cell populations, A cells subsequently emit a larger number of early spikes, due to a lower rheobase (documented by Hunt et al., 2018, Linaro et al., 2022, and our own data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)) and a steeper f-I curve (Hunt et al., 2018; Linaro et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational model with citations to previous research and the authors' own data.

claim: Initial spikes from A cells recruit many further A cells, due to the high A→A connectivity, but only a few T cells, due to the low A→T connectivity.
source: These initial spikes recruit many further A cells, due to the high A→A connectivity, but only a few T cells, due to the low A→T connectivity.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational model.

claim: A cells drive the growth of B cells, which in turn inhibit T cells, resulting in A cells having a net inhibitory effect on T cells.
source: On the other hand, A cells drive the growth of B cells, which in turn inhibit T cells (Figure 4Bi–ii): as a result, A cells have a net inhibitory effect on T cells, which get initially suppressed and can only start firing when the activity of A cells decreases, due to a surge in adaptation (Figure 4Biii).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational model shown in Figure 4Bi-ii and 4Biii.

claim: T cells get initially suppressed and can only start firing when the activity of A cells decreases, due to a surge in adaptation.
source: On the other hand, A cells drive the growth of B cells, which in turn inhibit T cells (Figure 4Bi–ii): as a result, A cells have a net inhibitory effect on T cells, which get initially suppressed and can only start firing when the activity of A cells decreases, due to a surge in adaptation (Figure 4Biii).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational model shown in Figure 4Bi-ii and 4Biii.

claim: The model dynamics result in clearly distinct peaks of A and T population activities, with an average delay of 29 ms between the peaks.
source: Together, these dynamics result in clearly distinct peaks of A and T population activities, with an average delay of 29 ms between the peaks (Figure 4Bi–ii).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational model shown in Figure 4Bi-ii.

claim: The long delay between A and T peaks matches the data by Hunt et al., 2018.
source: This long delay matches the data by Hunt et al., 2018, which would be hard to explain if T cells were directly recruited by A cells, with monosynaptic latencies shorter than three milliseconds (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous research with a citation and reference to the authors' own data.

claim: A decreased A→A or increased A→T connectivity would prevent the initial suppression of T cells, resulting in almost simultaneous peaks.
source: We confirm this intuition by varying each of the four connectivities in the model and find that a decreased A→A (Figure 4Ci) or increased A→T (Figure 4Cii) connectivity would indeed prevent the initial suppression of T cells, as activity would build up together in both populations, resulting in almost simultaneous peaks.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational model shown in Figure 4Ci and 4Cii.

claim: Further increasing A→A or decreasing A→T would more strongly suppress T cells, which could only fire after most A cells have adapted and fallen silent, with delays even over 100 ms.
source: On the contrary, further increasing A→A or decreasing A→T would more strongly suppress T cells, which could only fire after most A cells have adapted and fallen silent, with delays even over 100 ms.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational model.

claim: Connections from T neurons determine whether these provide net excitation or inhibition to A neurons, but cannot prevent the early activation of the A population.
source: Analogously, connections from T neurons determine whether these provide net excitation or inhibition to A neurons. However, albeit affecting the relative size of the A and T peaks, such connections on their own cannot prevent the early activation of the A population, which depends on single-neuron parameters.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational model.

claim: The model dynamics and the effects of excitatory-to-excitatory connectivities qualitatively remain unaltered if short-term depression and variability of synapses are included in the model.
source: The model dynamics and the effects of excitatory-to-excitatory connectivities qualitatively remain unaltered if we include in the model the experimentally observed short-term depression and variability of synapses (Figure 4—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational model shown in Figure 4—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: Long delays are consistently found when A→A is large and when A→T is small.
source: We find that long delays are consistently found when A→A is large (Figure 5A1,2,3) and when A→T is small (Figure 5A3,4,5), provided that delays do not become so long that population T does not activate at all.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational model shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Connections to the B interneurons have only a minor effect on the delay, while connections from the B interneurons are as important as the excitatory connections.
source: In this analysis, it clearly emerges that connections to the B interneurons have only a minor effect on the delay, while connections from the B interneurons are as important as the excitatory connections outlined above.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational model analysis.

claim: B interneurons optimally contribute to the suppression of T when they primarily target T rather than A.
source: In addition, we see that B interneurons optimally contribute to the suppression of T when they primarily target T (Figure 5B, fourth row and third column) rather than A (Figure 5B, third row and fourth column).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational model shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Not only can T cells activate after A cells even if the A→T connectivity is low, but such a low connectivity is also crucial to explain the delay seen in the data by Hunt et al., 2018 and in the model.
source: In conclusion, modeling shows that not only can T cells activate after A cells even if the A→T connectivity is low, but such a low connectivity is also crucial to explain the delay seen in the data by Hunt et al., 2018 and in our model.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the computational modeling with a citation to previous research.

claim: The connectivity between thorny and athorny classes is distinctly asymmetric, with athorny cells receiving ample input from themselves and thorny cells, but thorny cells receiving sparse inputs from athorny pyramids.
source: Moreover, we find that the connectivity between these classes is distinctly asymmetric, with athorny cells receiving ample input from themselves and thorny cells, but thorny cells receiving sparse inputs from athorny pyramids.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: Two other groups have recently reported similar findings using two different experimental methods, classifying cells by location in the pyramidal layer (deep and superficial) rather than thorny or athorny.
source: Though classified by location in the pyramidal layer (deep and superficial) rather than thorny or athorny, two other groups have recently reported similar findings using two different experimental methods (Watson et al., 2024; Layous et al., 2025).
evidence: This is a comparison to recent research supported by citations.

claim: Both studies report superficial neurons frequently innervating themselves and deep CA3 pyramids and much less frequent connectivity from deep to superficial cells.
source: Both studies report superficial neurons frequently innervating themselves and deep CA3 pyramids and much less frequent connectivity from deep to superficial cells.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from other studies.

claim: Asymmetric connectivity is crucial for SPW events to have two distinct peaks with only partially overlapping activity for the two pyramidal populations.
source: Our modeling shows that asymmetric connectivity is crucial for SPW events to have two distinct peaks with only partially overlapping activity for the two pyramidal populations, matching the data by Hunt et al., 2018.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the computational modeling with a citation to previous research.

claim: The long delay (tens of milliseconds) in the model is explained by the ambivalent role of athorny neurons, which on the one hand switch the network to the SPW state, but on the other hand initially disynaptically suppress the thorny neurons.
source: The long delay (tens of milliseconds) in our model is explained by the ambivalent role of athorny neurons, which on the one hand switch the network to the SPW state, but on the other hand initially disynaptically suppress the thorny neurons.
evidence: This is an explanation from the computational modeling.

claim: The switch to the SPW state occurs because PV+ basket cells take over from anti-SPW interneurons.
source: The switch to the SPW state occurs because PV+ basket cells take over from anti-SPW interneurons, a putative class proposed by Evangelista et al., 2020 to explain the paradoxical triggering of SPWs by in vitro stimulation of PV+ basket cells (Schlingloff et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an explanation from the computational modeling with citations to previous research.

claim: An interneuron class with similar properties to anti-SPW interneurons was identified in CA1.
source: Although their existence in CA3 still needs to be demonstrated, an interneuron class with similar properties was identified in CA1 (Dudok et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: During a SPW, the initial suppression of thorny neurons occurs through the shared pool of PV+ basket cells.
source: During a SPW, the initial suppression of thorny neurons occurs through the shared pool of PV+ basket cells.
evidence: This is an explanation from the computational modeling.

claim: The long delay observed in the model does not require special asymmetries in the connectivity between the interneurons and the pyramidal populations, given the measured values of excitatory connectivity.
source: The long delay that we observed in our model does not require special asymmetries in the connectivity between the interneurons and the pyramidal populations, given the measured values of excitatory connectivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the computational modeling.

claim: At least some baseline connectivity from athorny to basket and from basket to thorny neurons is required for the proposed disynaptic inhibition to exist.
source: However, at least some baseline connectivity from athorny to basket and from basket to thorny neurons is required for the proposed disynaptic inhibition to exist.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the computational modeling.

claim: The CA3 pyramidal population has two developmentally distinct groups — early-born and late-born cells.
source: The CA3 pyramidal population has two developmentally distinct groups — early-born and late-born cells (Marissal et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Developmentally distinct subpopulations have been shown to exhibit functionally different roles in memory encoding, with late-born cells recruited earlier in the encoding process than early-born cells.
source: These developmentally distinct subpopulations have been shown to exhibit functionally different roles in memory encoding, with late-born cells recruited earlier in the encoding process than early-born cells (Kveim et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Early-born neurons tend to be located closer to the stratum oriens and have longer primary apical dendrites.
source: Early-born neurons tend to be located closer to the stratum oriens and have longer primary apical dendrites (Marissal et al., 2012), reminiscent of our findings on athorny cells.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research and compared to the authors' findings.

claim: Modulation of thorn density has been reported through excessive training in spatial memory tasks and chemically via steroid hormones.
source: Moreover, modulation of thorn density has been reported through excessive training in spatial memory tasks and chemically via steroid hormones (Gómez-Padilla et al., 2020; Hatanaka et al., 2009; Tsurugizawa et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Connectivity between CA3 pyramids is asymmetric across subpopulations.
source: In line with recent evidence that the CA3 pyramidal population is non-homogeneous, we find that connectivity between these pyramids is asymmetric across subpopulations.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: The asymmetry in connectivity is key in maintaining the separation of peak firing between the two populations, thorny and athorny, during sharp wave events.
source: Our modeling work shows that this asymmetry is key in maintaining the separation of peak firing between the two populations, thorny and athorny, during sharp wave events.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the computational modeling.

claim: Mice used in the study were C57/Bl6n, bred in-house and originating from Charles River, P25+, average age: P40, both sexes.
source: Mice (C57/Bl6n, bred in-house and originating from Charles River, P25+, average age: P40, both sexes) were decapitated following isoflurane anesthesia.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods.

claim: Slices (400 µm) were cut in a horizontal plane on a vibratome.
source: Slices (400 µm) were cut in a horizontal plane on a vibratome (VT1200S; Leica) and stored in an interface chamber at 32–34 °C.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods.

claim: Recordings were performed in ACSF at 32–34°C in a submerged-type recording chamber.
source: Recordings were performed in ACSF at 32–34°C in a submerged-type recording chamber.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods.

claim: Somatic whole-cell patch-clamp recordings of up to eight cells were performed simultaneously.
source: We performed somatic whole-cell patch-clamp recordings (pipette resistance 3–5 MΩ) of up to eight cells simultaneously.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods.

claim: A subset of the data (n = 238 out of 348 cells) was published in a separate study.
source: A subset of the data (n = 238 out of 348 cells) was published in a separate study (Sammons et al., 2024).
evidence: This is a statement about data usage with a citation.

claim: Cells with a membrane potential less negative than −50 mV and a series resistance higher than 30 MΩ were discarded.
source: Cells with a membrane potential less negative than −50 mV and a series resistance higher than 30 MΩ were discarded.
evidence: This is a description of the data analysis methods.

claim: Neurons are modeled as adaptive exponential (AdEx) integrate-and-fire neurons.
source: Neurons are modeled as adaptive exponential (AdEx) integrate-and-fire neurons (Brette and Gerstner, 2005).
evidence: This is a description of the computational model with a citation.

claim: The AdEx model level of complexity (two dynamic variables: voltage and adaptation) is necessary to capture the diverse firing patterns of different neural populations.
source: This level of complexity (two dynamic variables: voltage and adaptation) is necessary to capture the diverse firing patterns of different neural populations.
evidence: This is a justification for the model choice.

claim: Neuronal adaptation has been proposed as the main mechanism governing the alternation between SPW and non-SPW states.
source: In addition, neuronal adaptation has been proposed as the main mechanism governing the alternation between SPW and non-SPW states (Levenstein et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: For A and T neurons, model parameters were chosen to be close to the single-neuron physiology following Hunt et al., 2018 and Linaro et al., 2022.
source: For A and T neurons, we follow the main figures and supplementary data by Hunt et al., 2018 and Linaro et al., 2022, since they performed detailed single-neuron physiological characterization of the two neuron types.
evidence: This is a description of the computational model parameters with citations.

claim: Athorny neurons were shown to have a higher input resistance, a higher resting potential, and a lower firing threshold than their thorny counterparts.
source: Namely, athorny neurons were shown to have a higher input resistance, a higher resting potential, and a lower firing threshold than their thorny counterparts, and both kinds have a high reset potential.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from previous research used to inform the model.

claim: Model parameters result in a lower rheobase for athorny than for thorny neurons.
source: Our parameters result in a lower rheobase for athorny than for thorny neurons (Hunt et al., 2018, Linaro et al., 2022, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result of the computational model with citations and reference to the authors' data.

claim: Interneuron parameters were based on data from CA3, if available, or otherwise from other hippocampal subfields.
source: Interneuron parameters were based on data from CA3, if available (Fidzinski et al., 2015; Pelkey et al., 2017), or otherwise from other hippocampal subfields (Ledri et al., 2012; Pawelzik et al., 2002; Tricoire et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a description of the computational model parameters with citations.

claim: Each population size is based on an estimation of its representation in a 400-µm-thick CA3 slice, according to the quantitative assessment by Bezaire and Soltesz, 2013.
source: Each population size is based on an estimation of its representation in a 400-µm-thick CA3 slice, according to the quantitative assessment by Bezaire and Soltesz, 2013.
evidence: This is a description of the computational model parameters with a citation.

claim: Pyramidal neurons are divided into thorny and athorny according to the 66–34% ratio that was determined experimentally.
source: Pyramidal neurons are divided into thorny and athorny according to the 66–34% ratio that we determined experimentally.
evidence: This is a description of the computational model parameters based on experimental data.

claim: For excitatory-to-excitatory connections, the probabilities have the values that were assessed experimentally.
source: For excitatory-to-excitatory connections, these probabilities have the values that we assessed experimentally.
evidence: This is a description of the computational model parameters based on experimental data.

claim: SPW events are identified based on the current flowing from B cells to the excitatory ones, which is thought to represent most of the LFP signal observed in the stratum pyramidale.
source: SPW events are identified based on the current flowing from B cells to the excitatory ones, which is thought to represent most of the LFP signal observed in the stratum pyramidale.
evidence: This is a description of the computational model analysis method.
